title: Why is "edit as new message" only available on a right-click menu on the body of an email?
creator: mark+mozilla
content:
The option "Edit as New Message" is only available when a user right-clicks on the body of an email.

The option is not available in the menu displayed from the "More" button on an email. The option is also not available in the right-click menu on an email in a mailbox list. The option is only available in the right-click menu from the body of an email.

Requiring a user to use the right-click option in a specific area of the user interface is an accessibility issue which should be fixed.

title: How can I whitelist email senders using message filters?
creator: rsberger1
content:
I understand that Thunderbird recommends managing spam by trusting senders in the Personal Address Book and/or Collected Addresses. For that to work, I would have to put the many companies who send me messages that I needn't reply to into the Personal Address Book. But I prefer to only put people I know into the Personal Address Book. So I looked for an alternative method of managing selected senders, and thought I had found one, but it's not working.

The alternative I thought I'd found was to use Message Filters. I created a filter I called "Whitelist", and in the Filter Rules dialog I said to apply the filter when it is run manually, or when getting new mail, and to apply the filter after spam classification (although when this didn't work, I also tried running the filter before spam classification). I said to apply the filter when the "from" address matches a sender that I wanted to whitelist. And I said to set the spam status for such messages to "Not Spam", and to move them to my inbox.

Nevertheless, emails from the sender I specified continued to be put into my spam folder.

Am I doing something wrong? If filter rules cannot be used to override automatic spam handling, why does the filter UI allow you to set the spam status to "Not Spam"?
